reason: In one session the same metaform memory notice ("N memories; N unread") re-fired after nearly every turn, and each time the agent re-read the same element's records and re-reported the same waiting items. A fields-filtered read also errored. No skill covers reading memory notices, so the rule lives in a new narrow skill.

The notice and the read disagree in a way the skill does not cover. In one agent session the notice said "3 unread, including 3 updated" repeatedly while triage returned nothing and view=full returned an updated entity; the skill only says to retry view=full "if needed", which gives no stopping rule.

Agents spent several turns re-reading and re-recording the same notice miscount, and one wrote a fourth duplicate observation about it. The skill needs a rule for what to do when the count does not match the read: trust the read, and do not add to the record.

A GC session read the node with must_contain filters several times while the notice kept reporting the same unread count; the filtered reads never cleared it. Durable read-pattern fact for this notice class.

The skill says not to re-read unchanged records, but in this episode the assistant re-read code.interface.graphical on nearly every turn, getting `{"entities":[],"relations":[]}` or `{}` each time, and replied "Nothing new: both reads came back empty." after each one. The rule needs to cover the cross-turn case explicitly and say that a repeated empty result is silence, not a status line.
Repeated identical unread notices kept triggering reads and a "Nothing new" reply even after empty reads; the existing rule says send no reply, so this makes the silent turn explicit.
The agent kept re-reading the same node across turns after several empty reads through different shapes (CLI, then MCP view=count), each followed by a reply. The stop rule covers only one shape.
Absorbed into the metaform-development umbrella under Memory notices and observations. No subfiles.
